RECO.why: Inline board marking is only auditable if every code is graded as it is made and failures are physically segregated.
OSAT and fab lines expect SECS/GEM handshakes and per-unit records; retrofitting them later means re-qualifying the tool.
Wafer and package tools sit inside classified space — particulate control has to be designed in, not added.
Cell-to-pack recall exposure is the reason to capture genealogy at the point of marking rather than reconstructing it later.
A weld you cannot measure is a weld you cannot warrant; monitoring turns each joint into inspectable data.
Copper welding is unstable at the melt boundary — depth monitoring is what makes the process capable rather than merely repeatable.
Electrode-area humidity degrades cell performance; the cell build must match the room it will live in.
Medical and hermetic work is audited on evidence, so e-signature controls and IQ/OQ/PQ belong in the machine scope from day one.
Marking, cutting and cleaning all generate process emissions; filtered extraction with flow monitoring is the baseline duty of care.
Fixture tolerance, not the scanner, usually limits mark placement — fiducial correction removes that variable.
Stepped and curved parts drift out of focus across the field; a 3-axis head holds spot size where a 2-axis head cannot.
Circumferential features need synchronised rotation to keep energy density constant around the part.
Diagnostics that need a site visit cost days; outbound telemetry resolves most faults the same shift.
An unshielded weld pool oxidises as it solidifies; the joint looks acceptable and fails on test.
Assist gas ejects the melt from the kerf — without it the cut redeposits and the edge closes behind the beam.
Above a kilowatt the process runs in keyhole; penetration cannot be inferred from the surface, so it has to be measured.
Real assemblies do not present zero gap; beam oscillation widens the fusion zone enough to tolerate the fit-up you actually get.
Thermal distortion moves the joint during the weld; a fixed path walks off it on long seams.
Spot size is only valid at focus; a part family with varying height loses fluence long before the operator sees a defect.
On a single-station table the machine waits for the operator; a second station returns that time to production.
Manual board loading is where inline traceability breaks down — magazine-to-magazine keeps the chain intact.
Singulated packages cannot be bulk fed without damage; tray handling preserves orientation and surface.
Foil and film arrive on a reel; cutting them as sheets adds a conversion step the process does not need.
A turntable keeps the operator outside the guarded volume while the cell runs, which is what makes the interlock scheme workable.
Lithium-bearing assemblies react with atmospheric moisture during processing; an inert backfill is a process requirement, not a precaution.
A CE-marked laser inside an integrated cell does not make the cell compliant — the conformity file has to cover the machine as delivered.
Medical and implant-adjacent production is audited on documented evidence; retrofitting IQ/OQ/PQ after installation repeats the qualification.
